rationale: Verified 11 blocking defects directly against source: two critical stacktrace-leak gaps survive this round's HIDE_AGENT_STREAMING_EXCEPTIONS redaction fix (the INTERNAL-category error path in langgraph_agent.py/core/errors.py, and the queue-timeout path in _build_timeout_result), plus a missing timeout guard on the A2A streaming path, an unclamped/uncached queue-poll config lookup, a parallel-vs-sequential tool-error counting gap, an echo-dedup dict-drop bug, a timeout that doesn't cancel the underlying agent run, and a commit-format standards violation on 2 commits. 2 findings (subagent-mode chunk unpacking, cross-author _inflight_run_ids leak) have unconfirmed live-path reachability and are capped at major. No spec/story exists for this range, so acceptance did not run (confidence floored at low) and decision_needed is unavailable; 2 lens reports were dismissed as noise after verification (a self-documented, deliberate error-classifier string coupling, and a _build_final_chunk/last_generation_result removal confirmed dead-code-only via git history and the change's own planning artifacts).

standards_review.notes: 2 commits use a lowercase branch-slug prefix instead of `EPMCDME-####:`; 1 merge commit also off-format.
Modern parameterized type hints throughout; new test files carry the required Apache 2.0 header.
No credential/token logging found; scope limited to secret-handling and untrusted-input rules, not the stacktrace-leak findings raised by other lenses.

findings.file: commit "epmcdme-14855-token-limit-slice2: add planning artifacts" / "epmcdme-14855-graph-cancellation-core: add planning artifacts"
findings.title: Commit subjects break ticket-format rule
findings.problem: Two commits use a lowercase branch-slug prefix ('epmcdme-14855-<slice>:') instead of the git-workflow.md-required `EPMCDME-####: Description` subject format.
findings.impact: Violates the repo's blocking commit-format standard, breaking tooling/traceability that expects a ticket-prefixed subject on every commit in the range.
findings.recommendation: Reword both subjects to `EPMCDME-14855: <description>` (e.g. via rebase) before merge.

findings.title: _inflight_run_ids leak on author mismatch
findings.problem: on_tool_error/on_tool_end discard a run_id only from `_inflight_run_ids[author]` keyed by that callback's own author; if on_tool_start recorded the run_id under a different author, it is never removed from the original bucket.
findings.impact: Reachability unconfirmed (uncertain, capped at major): if it occurs, the stale run_id keeps the original author's bucket permanently non-empty, so on_tool_error treats that author's future genuine sequential retries as concurrent and stops aliasing them onto one visible thought.
findings.recommendation: Discard the run_id from every author bucket in `_inflight_run_ids`, not only the bucket keyed by the current callback's author.

findings.title: InternalError path still leaks full stack trace
findings.problem: The new stacktrace redaction in `_send_error_to_thread` is gated on `error_response.category == ErrorCategory.AGENT`. An unclassified exception is routed by `InternalErrorClassifier` to `category=INTERNAL`, whose `InternalError.details['traceback']` (core/errors.py `InternalError.from_exception`) is never touched by that redaction.
findings.impact: When `config.HIDE_AGENT_STREAMING_EXCEPTIONS=True`, an unclassified exception still ships `error_details` containing the full raw Python traceback to the client in the SSE chunk, defeating the exact protection this round added for the AGENT category. Verified directly in core/errors.py:293-374 and langgraph_agent.py:865-879.
findings.recommendation: Extend the redaction to the INTERNAL category: strip/redact `details.traceback` on the InternalError payload the same way `agent_error.stacktrace` is redacted, before building error_details.

findings.title: _check_truncation_in_chunk assumes chunk shape
findings.problem: `if self.subagents: _, *chunk = chunk` followed by `chunk_type, value = chunk` assumes every incoming chunk is a 3-tuple whenever `self.subagents` is truthy; a 2-tuple chunk in that mode leaves only one element after the strip.
findings.impact: Reachability unconfirmed (uncertain, capped at major): if a subagent-mode stream ever yields a plain 2-tuple, the unpack raises `ValueError: not enough values to unpack` from inside the streaming loop, aborting the stream.
findings.recommendation: Guard the unpack (e.g. check `len(chunk) == 2` before assuming a namespace prefix was stripped) instead of unconditionally unpacking.

findings.title: Tool-error counter doesn't distinguish parallel batches
findings.problem: `_on_tool_error` increments a single per-author scalar (`_consecutive_tool_error_count[author]`) on every tool-error callback with no concurrent-vs-sequential distinction, unlike the new `_inflight_run_ids`/`_active_error_streak` mechanism this same diff adds to `AgentStreamingCallback` for exactly that purpose.
findings.impact: When one author's LLM turn issues several parallel tool calls (parallel_tool_calls is only disabled per-model, not globally — langgraph_agent.py:301-306) that all fail in the same round, each failure still increments the same counter, so MaxConsecutiveToolErrorsExceededException can fire after a single bad parallel batch instead of after N genuinely consecutive attempts.
findings.recommendation: Have `_on_tool_error` consult the same in-flight/concurrent-siblings signal the callback now tracks before incrementing the abort counter, so concurrent failures in one round count once, not once per tool call.

findings.title: Echo-dedup guard drops whole update, not just the echo
findings.problem: `if author is None and any(key in self.agent.subagent_descriptions for key in value): return` discards the entire `value` dict as soon as any one key matches a subagent name, even when `value` also carries other, unrelated top-level keys in the same update tick.
findings.impact: A mixed update — a legitimate top-level node key plus a subagent-named echo key arriving together — has the legitimate key's state update silently dropped along with the echo, not just the echo itself.
findings.recommendation: Drop only the matched subagent-name keys from `value` before processing, rather than returning on any single match.

findings.title: Queue-poll timeout has no floor/clamp
findings.problem: `_get_queue_poll_timeout_seconds()` returns the dynamic-config value unclamped, unlike the sibling `_get_max_consecutive_tool_errors()` (langgraph_agent.py:141-149) which explicitly applies `max(1, value)`.
findings.impact: If `AI_AGENT_QUEUE_POLL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` is ever set to 0 or negative, `queue.Queue.get(timeout=...)` either busy-loops (timeout=0, since the surrounding while-loop retries immediately) or raises an uncaught ValueError for a negative timeout — neither is caught by the `except queue.Empty:` handler in `_serve_data`/`HedgedAssistantHandler`.
findings.recommendation: Clamp the resolved value with `max(1, value)` the same way `_get_max_consecutive_tool_errors` does.

findings.title: Queue-poll timeout re-resolved every chunk
findings.problem: `_get_queue_poll_timeout_seconds()` is called fresh on every loop iteration in both `StandardAssistantHandler._serve_data` (line 763) and `HedgedAssistantHandler._stream_agent_path` (hedged_handler.py:394), with no caching, unlike the analogous `_max_consecutive_tool_errors_cache` this same diff adds for the tool-error-cap lookup.
findings.impact: The queue-timeout lookup sits on a hotter path (once per streamed chunk) than the tool-error cap (once per tool failure) yet has no equivalent protection, hitting DynamicConfigService on every SSE chunk under load.
findings.recommendation: Cache the resolved timeout on the handler instance on first use, mirroring `_max_consecutive_tool_errors_cache`.

findings.title: Timeout doesn't stop the still-running agent
findings.problem: `_build_timeout_result` closes `generator_queue` so the producer thread's future sends become no-ops, but nothing cancels or interrupts the underlying LangGraph run/LLM calls still executing on that producer thread.
findings.impact: The client receives a terminal timeout chunk while the abandoned agent run keeps executing to completion in the background, continuing to consume LLM/compute spend for a request nobody is listening to.
findings.recommendation: Signal the producer thread/task to cancel (e.g. propagate a cancellation token or close the underlying LangGraph run) when the queue-poll timeout fires, not just the reporting queue.

findings.title: Timeout path skips stacktrace redaction
findings.problem: `_build_timeout_result` builds `agent_error`/`error_details` via `_format_errors(error_response, ...)` and `agent_error.model_dump(mode="json")` directly, without applying the `HIDE_AGENT_STREAMING_EXCEPTIONS` redaction that `_send_error_to_thread` (langgraph_agent.py:867-872) applies to the identical fields; it also derives `error_details` from `agent_error` alone instead of the full `error_response.get_error()` payload the other path uses.
findings.impact: When an operator sets `HIDE_AGENT_STREAMING_EXCEPTIONS=True`, a queue-poll timeout on the Standard or Hedged streaming path still ships a populated raw stacktrace inside agent_error/error_details in the client-visible SSE chunk, undermining the redaction this same diff added for the generic-exception path.
findings.recommendation: Route `_build_timeout_result` through the same redaction logic as `_send_error_to_thread` (strip stacktrace under HIDE_AGENT_STREAMING_EXCEPTIONS) and build error_details from the same payload source for both paths.

findings.title: A2A stream_generator has no queue timeout
findings.problem: `A2AAssistantHandler.stream_generator` still calls `generator_queue.queue.get()` with no timeout, unlike `StandardAssistantHandler._serve_data` (line 763) and `HedgedAssistantHandler._stream_agent_path` (hedged_handler.py:394), which this same diff converted to a bounded `get(timeout=...)` plus a `queue.Empty` branch.
findings.impact: If the remote A2A task producer never invokes `task_callback` with `final=True` — the exact abandoned-producer failure mode this diff's fix targets on the other two paths — the A2A streaming request's consumer thread blocks indefinitely instead of surfacing a timeout error to the client.
findings.recommendation: Adopt the same `timeout=self._get_queue_poll_timeout_seconds()` plus queue.Empty/_build_timeout_result-style handling in stream_generator's queue-read loop.
